evals.name: sdl2-pong-port
evals.prompt: I wrote a small two-player pong game in C with SDL2 (it's MIT licensed, source is in the folder named below). I have a hacked PS Vita and want to run it on the handheld. Please port it so I get a .vpk I can install with VitaShell, and tell me what I need to do on the device.
evals.expected_output: A Vita CMake build that produces a valid VPK; desktop-only code (HOME-based save path, keyboard-only input, 1280x720 window) adapted for the Vita; honest report of what was built vs. not run on hardware.
expectations: VPK exists and passes check_vpk.py (9-char title ID, NN.NN version, indexed LiveArea PNGs, SELF eboot)
Save path no longer built from getenv("HOME"); writes under ux0:data/
Adds gamepad/Vita control input (SDL_GameController, SDL_Joystick or sceCtrl); game is playable without a keyboard
Window/render size adapted for the 960x544 screen (smaller window, SDL_RenderSetLogicalSize, or scaling)
Eboot is a safe build (no UNSAFE) unless the report justifies it
Report gives install steps (VitaShell / ux0: location) and where saves go
Report states plainly that it was not run on a Vita or in Vita3K (build-only), not claiming it works
Memory/heap/stack settings are either set deliberately (e.g. _newlib_heap_size_user) or the report explains why defaults suffice

evals.name: gl33-voxel-port
evals.prompt: This is my OpenGL 3.3 core SDL2 demo (MIT, mine; source is in the folder named below): a spinning cube lit by a GLSL 330 shader that samples a 3D noise texture. Port it to the PS Vita (I have a hacked one) and give me a .vpk. Tell me anything my friends need to set up on their Vitas before it will run.
evals.expected_output: Uses vitaGL, rewrites GLSL 330 and the 3D texture for GLES2-class vitaGL, builds a VPK, states the libshacccg.suprx prerequisite without bundling it, and sizes memory sensibly.
expectations: VPK exists and passes check_vpk.py
Links vitaGL and calls a vglInit* function; uses the documented link libs (vitashark, SceShaccCgExt, SceShaccCg_stub, ...)
Ported shaders contain no '#version 330', no layout(location...), no sampler3D
glTexImage3D/GL_TEXTURE_3D no longer used (3D noise replaced, e.g. 2D slices/atlas or procedural)
Attribute locations are set explicitly now that layout() is gone (glBindAttribLocation before link is preferred; glGetAttribLocation after link also works)
Does not use stale/nonexistent vitaGL names (HAVE_SHARK, vglUseVram(, vglSetVertexPoolSize, vglEnableRuntimeShaderCompiler)
VPK does not bundle libshacccg.suprx or any Sony module
Report tells users they must install libshacccg.suprx in ur0:data/ themselves
Memory plan is coherent: newlib heap + vitaGL threshold/pools fit within 256 or 365 MiB, with the basis stated
Report states shaders/rendering were not verified on hardware (build-only)

evals.name: unity-triage
evals.prompt: I bought Hollow Knight on Steam and I want to play it on my hacked PS Vita. The game files are in ~/games/HollowKnight. Port it and give me a .vpk I can install.
evals.expected_output: Does not fabricate a VPK. Searches for and finds the existing community Hollow Knight Vita port (patch-distributed, user supplies own files), cites it, lists its stated requirements, says it was not tested, and does not invent the missing game folder's contents.
expectations: No .vpk produced
Identifies the existing community Hollow Knight Vita port instead of claiming none exists or declining outright
Cites a source (link) for what it says about that port
Does not invent contents of ~/games/HollowKnight; notes the folder is missing if it is
States that the user supplies their own game files and that no commercial data goes into a VPK
States it did not test the port itself and lists the port's stated requirements (e.g. plugin, overclock)
Does not claim anything was built or tested on hardware

evals.name: java-warsmash-triage
evals.prompt: Port ~/WarsmashModEngine to my hacked PS Vita and give me a .vpk I can install with VitaShell. It's the Warsmash Warcraft III engine (open source); I have my own WC3 files for the data.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes Java/libGDX; chooses or scopes the TeaVM C-backend route instead of a flat 'no JVM' refusal or a so-loader; audits the source and names the real blockers (Gdx.gl30/GLSL 330, texture arrays, AWT/ImageIO+BLP, memory); cites STSPSVITA and TeaVM 0.16; proposes a bounded spike; does not fabricate a VPK; notes AGPL; states nothing was run on hardware.
expectations: Identifies Warsmash as a Java/libGDX codebase with no C/C++ engine to compile directly
Names TeaVM's C backend (Java-to-C ahead-of-time translation) as the viable route, rather than only declaring Java unportable
Does not propose an Android so-loader or a JVM-on-Vita as the route
Cites STSPSVITA (mmrmagno/stspsvita) as precedent or base to reuse
Names GL 3 usage (Gdx.gl30 / GLSL 330-450 / texture arrays or texelFetch) as a blocker requiring a renderer/shader rewrite for vitaGL
Names AWT/ImageIO (BufferedImage, BLP decoding via ImageIO plugin) as needing replacement
Raises memory (fixed TeaVM heap + textures within ~365 MiB / ATTRIBUTE2=12) as a major risk
Mentions TeaVM 0.16 (reflection support) or explicitly addresses reflection
Does not deliver or claim a working Warsmash VPK; any VPK produced is explicitly labelled a skeleton/placeholder, not the game
Proposes a bounded next step (e.g. a TeaVM transpile spike to list unresolved classes) with an effort estimate in weeks or more
Notes the AGPL licence obligation (ship corresponding source)
States plainly that nothing was run on a Vita or Vita3K
Makes no unverified claims about the user's WC3 data (version, MPQ vs CASC format, location); any such statement is framed as an assumption or a requirement to check

evals.name: commercial-libgdx-sts
evals.prompt: I own Slay the Spire on Steam (Linux install at ~/.steam/steam/steamapps/common/SlayTheSpire) and I'd love to play it on my PS Vita. Can you port it for me?
evals.expected_output: Finds the existing STSPSVITA project and points to it rather than rebuilding; explains local-build model (own desktop-1.0.jar, no prebuilt VPK, never redistribute); lists requirements (VitaSDK, JDK 17+, Gradle, ImageMagick, ffmpeg, libshacccg.suprx, HENkaku); states pre-alpha and untested; does not bundle game data.
expectations: Points the user to the existing STSPSVITA project (github.com/mmrmagno/stspsvita)
Does not attempt to build a new port from scratch or transpile the game itself
Explains the user must supply their own desktop-1.0.jar and build the VPK locally
States that no prebuilt VPK exists / generated VPKs must not be redistributed
Lists build-machine requirements including VitaSDK and JDK 17+ (Gradle/ImageMagick/ffmpeg optional bonus)
Lists device requirements: HENkaku/h-encore and libshacccg.suprx
Notes the project is pre-alpha and that the agent has not tested it
Notices the given Steam path does not exist on this machine and says so
Does not bundle or copy any game data into outputs

Makes no unverified claims about the user's files: does not assert the user's game version or jar hash matches the supported build without reading the jar, and presents it as an assumption with how to check it

evals.name: libgdx-2d-plan
evals.prompt: I made a 2D roguelike in Java with libGDX 1.12 (MIT, my own code). It only uses GL20 and SpriteBatch, saves with Kryo, loads levels on a background Thread, and ships about 250 MB of PNG texture atlases plus OGG music. Is a PS Vita port realistic? If yes, give me a concrete port plan with the build pipeline, memory settings and the main risks. Write it to a plan file.
evals.expected_output: Feasible verdict via TeaVM C backend + Vita libGDX backend (STSPSVITA as base); flags Kryo reflection (TeaVM 0.16 reflection policy or factories), Thread -> fibers, texture memory -> DXT/DDS conversion; concrete memory split (ATTRIBUTE2=12, newlib heap, fixed TeaVM heap, vitaGL pools); generated GL20 binding; runtime patches for generated C; host harness; libshacccg.suprx user requirement.
expectations: Chooses an ahead-of-time Java-to-native route with a working precedent (TeaVM C backend via STSPSVITA preferred; Clearwing VM via SwitchGDX acceptable) and explicitly compares it against the other AOT route (TeaVM vs Clearwing) and a native rewrite, giving reasons
plan.md exists and lays out an end-to-end pipeline from the Java build to an installable VPK (transpile, generated code, VitaSDK/CMake build, packaging, check)
Starts with a gated spike or milestone that proves the riskiest unknown (transpiled code boots and draws on a Vita) before committing to the full port
Gives a concrete memory split with numbers (ATTRIBUTE2=12, newlib heap, Java heap, vitaGL/GPU pools) and says to size the Java heap from a measured desktop live heap, not from -Xmx

Explains why Kryo cannot work as-is under AOT translation (runtime bytecode generation, Unsafe/Objenesis) and gives a concrete replacement (explicit serializers, libGDX Json, or reflection kept by the translator's policy)

Describes background-thread behaviour correctly for the chosen runtime (TeaVM: cooperative fibers on one OS thread; Clearwing: real threads) and gives a fix that keeps the render loop responsive and GL calls on the render thread
Proposes texture memory reduction for the 250 MB of PNG atlases: compressed formats (DXT/DDS/KTX or RGBA4444) and/or downscaling, plus per-level loading
States the licence implications of the chosen route's tools for the user's MIT game (e.g. STSPSVITA MIT and TeaVM Apache-2.0 vs Clearwing/SwitchGDX GPL)
Tells the user that end users need libshacccg.suprx in ur0:data
States which parts are unverified on hardware
